{
  "hypotheses": [
    {
      "hypothesis_id": "H1",
      "hypothesis": "Subject-specific baseline heart rate variability influences conformal prediction coverage stability.",
      "proposed_mechanism": "Higher baseline HRV leads to larger prediction errors, causing conformal intervals to be too narrow and resulting in under-coverage.",
      "causal_path": "baseline_HRV -> prediction_error_magnitude -> interval_width -> coverage_rate",

        "baseline_HRV",
        "prediction_error_magnitude",
        "interval_width",
        "coverage_rate"

        "age",
        "medication_use",
        "signal_quality"
      ],
      "control_variables": [
        "age",
        "medication_use"
      ],
      "rival_explanation": "Coverage fluctuations are due to random noise in the conformal algorithm rather than subject traits.",
      "rival_prediction": "Coverage variability will be uncorrelated with baseline HRV across subjects.",
      "distinguishing_test": "If coverage correlates negatively with baseline HRV after controlling for age and medication, the mechanism is supported; if no correlation, the rival is supported.",
      "effect_size_expectation": "medium",
      "effect_size_rationale": "Prior work shows moderate association between HRV and prediction error in physiological signals.",
      "minimum_data_needed": [
        "baseline_HRV_measurements",
        "physiological_signal_segments",
        "conformal_prediction_outputs",
        "coverage_labels"

      "statistical_test_plan": "Linear mixed-effects model with coverage as outcome, baseline_HRV as fixed effect, subject as random effect, controlling for age and medication.",

    },
